title: Example: local sentiment analysis (VADER default, optional GoEmotions transformer)
description: Sentiment scoring as an example consumer; VADER as the default local backend, GoEmotions transformer optional behind the metrics extra. Done when: the example runs on fixtures with VADER and documents the optional transformer path.

comments.author: home
comments.text: home: Sentiment example landed at examples/sentiment/ — scoring.rs is a self-contained VADER-style backend (trimmed valence lexicon for coding-session vocabulary, caps emphasis, negation window, intensifiers, VADER compound normalization with 0.05 thresholds), fully in-process: classify(&str) -> Positive/Negative/Neutral. examples/sentiment/main.rs walks the committed corpus via examples/common (shared corpus walker extracted from the meter example) and prints per-session plus aggregate sentiment, documenting the planned GoEmotions transformer backend behind an optional botspy[metrics] extra (seam noted in scoring.rs, default stays local VADER). scoring.rs compiles into the BDD step crate via #[path] so the scenario exercises the real example logic; 'works fine' stays neutral per spec (weak valence words deliberately absent). consumers.feature @wip fully lifted: all four consumer scenarios executable and green (118 scenarios / 448 steps): 1 positive / 1 negative / 1 neutral on the spec session, and 'no message text leaves the machine' proven by a network-capability scan of every example source plus pure in-process scoring. Full gate green: fmt, clippy -D warnings, doc -D warnings, 8 doc tests, BDD 24/118/448, spec_docs_coverage, 37 lib tests, fixture corpus guards, both examples run.

right_now_summary: The example uses VADER by default, with an optional GoEmotions transformer path.
